sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

By way of the present application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the applicants- accused have prayed for anticipatory bail in connection with the FIR being No.11195035231040 of 2023 registered with Palanpur Taluka Police Station, Dist.Banaskantha for the offences punishable under Sections 307, 342, 328, 323, 498A, 506(2) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Heard learned advocate Mr.Rajan Patel for the applicants.
2.1
He submitted that the present applicants happen to be uncle-in-law and son-in-law respectively of the first informant who were living separately from the first informant and her husband.
The applicants have been falsely implicated in the present offence.

The applicants had merely NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22221/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/12/2023 undefined accompanied the Jayantibhai Laxmichand Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131732591/

sentences.text: 1 husband of the first informant in finding out the first informant herself.
Except these, no other overtact has been attributed to any of the present applicant in offence in question.
The applicant no.1, who is uncle-in-law of first informant is a senior citizen and applicant no.2, who is brother- in-law of the first informant, is a son of the present applicant no.1.
He, therefore, submitted to allow the present application and grant anticipatory bail to the present applicants.
2.2 Learned advocate for the applicants has further argued that the applicants will keep themselves available during the course of investigation and trial also and will not flee from justice.

2.3 Learned advocate for the applicants, on instructions , states that the applicants are ready and willing to abide by all the conditions including imposition of conditions with regard to powers of Investigating Agency to file an application before the competent Court for his remand.
He further submitted that upon filing of such application by the Investigating Agency, the right of applicant accused to oppose such application on merits may be kept open.

Learned advocate, therefore,
submitted that considering the above facts, the applicants may be granted anticipatory bail.

3.1 Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail, inter alia, contending that the applicants herein have played active role in commission of offence and, therefore, present application should be dismissed.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22221/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/12/2023 undefined

3.2 Learned advocate Mr.Bhavik Patel for the original first informant has also opposed the present application contending that present applicants had caught hold the first informant while her husband had administered sleeping pills to her.
He, therefore, submitted to dismiss the present application.

4. Heard learned advocates for the parties and perused the record.
5.1
The present applicant no.1 happens to be uncle of husband of the first informant.
As per case of the prosecution, on the day of Diwali, the first informant had left the house herself and posted a message in whats-up group of her family that she was going to commit suicide.
Therefore, the present applicants had accompanied the husband of the first informant for finding her out.
5.2 It is stated in the FIR that the present applicants had caught hold of the first informant whereas her husband had administered sleeping pills to her forcibly.
However, the present applicants are living separately from the first informant and her husband and other family members. .

5.3 This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors., reported at [2011] 1 SCC 694, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court reiterated the law laid down NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/22221/2023 ORDER DATED: 14/12/2023 undefined by the Constitution Bench in the case of Shri Gurubaksh Singh Sibbia & Ors. Vs. State of Punjab, reported at (1980) 2 SCC 565.

sentences.text: In the result, the present application is allowed.
This would be sufficient to treat the accused in the judicial custody for the purpose of entertaining application of the prosecution for police remand.

This is, however, without prejudice to the right of the accused to seek stay against an order of remand, if, ultimately, granted, and the power of the learned Magistrate to consider such a request in accordance with law.

It is clarified that the applicants, even if, remanded to the police custody, upon completion of such period of police remand, shall be set free immediately, subject to other conditions of this anticipatory bail order.
